Coverage is planned, with explicitly named geometric supplier/proof gaps; closure is not claimed.

nodes.title: Finite diagram endomorphisms in the native representation category
nodes.statement: For a field K and a diagram D represented by T in finite-dimensional K-vector spaces, the algebra E_F of the existing endomorphism-coalgebra node, for a finite subdiagram F, is the subalgebra of the product of End_K(T(v)) cut out by T(e) a_v = a_w T(e) for every edge e:v→w in F. It is naturally isomorphic to the categorical endomorphism algebra of the extended functor Paths(F)→ModuleCat(K), and is finite-dimensional. Restriction along F⊆G is a unital algebra homomorphism E_G→E_F; no surjectivity is asserted. Finite here means finitely many vertices and a finite set of constraints, or all constraints on those vertices: over K their common kernel is already cut out by finitely many constraints.

sources.locator: Definition 7.1.8 and Remark 7.1.9, pp. 136–137; Definition 7.1.10 and Remark 7.1.11, pp. 137–138
sources.match: The finite construction is the algebra of compatible vertex endomorphisms; passing to paths imposes no extra conditions.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.6, pp. 13–15
sources.match: Finite diagram endomorphisms form a finite algebra inside a product of module endomorphisms.

proofSteps: Use the existing representation carrier, not a second category of quiver representations. A natural endomorphism is exactly its family of vertex maps satisfying edge naturality.
Composition agrees with CategoryTheory.End multiplication: the later factor acts first in the written product a b = a∘b. Restrict families to define transition maps.

Embed E_F linearly in the finite product of finite-dimensional endomorphism spaces. For infinitely many edge constraints on a finite vertex set, finite-dimensional descending-chain stabilization gives an equivalent finite constraint set.
acceptance: The family model is the existing endomorphism-algebra construction expressed on native carriers.

nodes.title: Left modules and right finite-dual comodules
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional unital K-algebra E, the dual vector space E∨ has comultiplication dual to multiplication and counit evaluation at 1. Finite-dimensional left E-modules are equivalent, over their underlying K-vector spaces, to TauCeti.FGComoduleCat K E∨ of right comodules. For a basis (e_i) of E with dual basis (e_i∨), the coaction is m↦Σ_i e_i m⊗e_i∨. Applied to E_F, this identifies the finite module model of C(F,T) with the existing finite-comodule carrier. The equivalence intertwines restriction of scalars along E_G→E_F with corestriction along E_F∨→E_G∨.

sources.match: The adjunction between a finite projective algebra action and a right coaction on its dual gives the equivalence and its variance.
The finite equivalence is the first step of the diagram-coalgebra description.

proofSteps: Dualize the algebra laws using the finite-dimensional tensor-dual isomorphism; do not equip an arbitrary infinite algebra dual with this coalgebra structure.
Check the coaction formula is independent of the basis via the action–coaction adjunction. Transposing the two coaction identities recovers the two module identities.
On morphisms both functors retain the linear map; the action relation is equivalent to the coaction relation. Apply the same adjunction to an algebra map to check transition compatibility.
acceptance: For E=K the coaction is m↦m⊗1.
For E=K×K the two orthogonal idempotents give the two homogeneous components of a comodule.
For E=Mat_2(K) its standard column module uses the displayed order of multiplication; replacing E by its opposite without changing the action fails this check.

nodes.title: Finite support descent for the Nori coalgebra
nodes.statement: Let (A_i) be a filtered system of K-coalgebras and let A be its coalgebra colimit, whose underlying vector space is the filtered colimit. Every finite-dimensional right A-comodule is corestricted from a finite-dimensional A_i-comodule at some index. Every comodule map between two such objects is represented at a common later index; equality of two represented maps holds at a common later index whenever it holds over A. Consequently the 2-colimit of the finite-comodule categories is equivalent to FGComoduleCat K A. In particular A(D,T)=colim_F E_F∨ gives the existing diagram category, with faithful exact forgetful functor. Neither the coalgebra transition maps nor the algebra restriction maps need be injective or surjective.

sources.locator: Corollary 7.5.7 and its proof, pp. 170–172
sources.match: Finite comodules descend through the filtered coalgebra system and recover the diagram category.
The statement identifies the filtered diagram category with the comodule category.

proofSteps: Choose a basis of a finite-dimensional V. Its finitely many coaction coefficients lift simultaneously to some A_i.

Counitality and coassociativity are finitely many equations. A⊗A and higher finite tensor powers commute with filtered colimits over K, so all these equations hold at a later common index. This step is essential when transitions are not monomorphisms.
A linear map has finitely many entries; its coaction-compatibility equations descend in the same way. Equality of represented maps is eventual equality, not equality at their initial index.

At a finite stage E_F embeds as a left E_F-module into a finite sum of vertex modules by simultaneous evaluation on bases. Every finite E_F-module is a quotient of finitely many regular modules. Thus every diagram object is a subquotient of a finite sum of vertices, independently of universality.

Use these statements for essential surjectivity and full faithfulness of the 2-colimit comparison. Abelian/exact structure comes from the existing finite-comodule result, rather than a new comodule theory.
acceptance: A one-vertex diagram gives the finite-dual equivalence without a limit.
Adjoining an identity edge changes neither end algebra nor coalgebra.
Adding an edge may kill coalgebra coefficients: the argument must still descend equations at a later stage.

nodes.title: Reconstruction of an abelian category from its faithful fibre
nodes.statement: Let A be an essentially small K-linear abelian category with a faithful exact K-linear functor U:A→Vect_fd(K). Regard a small skeleton of A, with all of its morphisms, as a diagram. The canonical functor A→C(A,U) is an equivalence over Vect_fd(K). This is reconstruction of the abelian category, prior to any tensor or rigidity assertion.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1.20, p. 142; Lemma 7.3.16, pp. 155–158; Proposition 7.3.18 and proof of Theorem 7.1.20, pp. 158–160
sources.match: The finite regular-module object and compatible finite-piece functors prove full faithfulness and essential surjectivity.

sources.locator: Satz 3.28, p. 55, with Satz 3.27, pp. 51–55
sources.match: The thesis supplies the reconstruction equivalence used to obtain universality.

proofSteps: For an object p, finite copowers and kernels give the internal object Hom_K(U(p),p). Impose the finitely many commutator equations for End_A(p) to construct X(p) with fibre E(p), the centralizer algebra.
Composition equips X(p) with a right E(p)-action. Cokernels of finite presentations define X(p)⊗_{E(p)}M internally in A; no arbitrary cocompleteness is needed.
Evaluation X(p)⊗_{E(p)}U(p)→p is an actual map. Its fibre is the usual evaluation isomorphism, so faithful exactness reflects its being an isomorphism.

The constructions are compatible under p↦p⊕q. Pass to the filtered diagram categories of the additive/subquotient hulls, as in the cited proof. This constructs the inverse functor and proves fullness; faithfulness alone never supplies a lift of a linear map.
acceptance: For A=Vect_fd(K), the reconstruction recovers A, not the category of all vector spaces.
For A the finite left modules of a finite-dimensional algebra and U the forgetful functor, the regular module detects the full action.
The proof explicitly constructs X(p); it does not assume that every U-linear map is motivic.

nodes.title: Universal factorisation with specified fibre compatibility
nodes.statement: For a diagram representation T:D→Vect_fd(K), an essentially small K-linear abelian category A, a faithful exact U:A→Vect_fd(K), a representation F:D→A and a specified isomorphism U F≅T, there is a faithful exact K-linear L:C(D,T)→A, a lift isomorphism L T̃≅F, and a fibre isomorphism U L≅ω compatible with the specified diagram isomorphism. The groupoid of such compatible factorizations is contractible: the comparison isomorphism is unique over the specified fibre data and diagram lift. This does not assert unique arbitrary automorphisms of an unmarked functor.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1.13 and Corollary 7.1.15, pp. 138–140; Propositions 7.4.1–7.4.2, pp. 164–165
sources.match: Functoriality in diagrams followed by reconstruction gives existence; generation and faithful fibre compatibility give uniqueness.
The thesis proves the factorisation property after reconstruction of the target category.

proofSteps: Transport the specified isomorphism to compare T with U F. Diagram functoriality gives C(D,T)→C(A,U). Compose with the inverse of the reconstruction equivalence.
The resulting functor is exact and faithful because both constructions commute with the faithful exact fibres.

For two factorizations, compare on vertex objects and then finite sums, kernels and cokernels using generation. Faithfulness gives uniqueness for maps whose fibre is prescribed; check independence of finite presentations and compatibility on overlap.
Apply the same uniqueness to composites to obtain the equivalence of any two marked universal categories.
acceptance: The identity factorisation of C(D,T) is recovered up to the specified unique isomorphism.
A zero-valued diagram gives the zero abelian category.
Changing an unmarked fibre identification is not erased by the uniqueness claim.

nodes.title: Finite Betti cohomology of algebraic pairs
nodes.statement: For a reduced separated finite-type k-scheme X, a closed reduced subscheme Y and an embedding k↪C, H^i(X(C),Y(C);Q) is finite-dimensional and vanishes outside a finite nonnegative range. A finite family of closed subvarieties can be treated by compatible semialgebraic triangulation after compactification; this gives the relative finite-type and closed-cover excision statements needed below. X(C) need not itself be the realization of a finite simplicial complex: nonproper spaces need an open-subcomplex or finite CW homotopy model.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.6.10, p. 66, and Note 2.6.11; relative deformation-retraction argument in the proof of Proposition 2.6.9, pp. 67–70; Corollary 2.6.14, p. 70
sources.match: Compatible semialgebraic triangulation and the singular comparison give finiteness for pairs.

proofSteps: Apply complex analytification from its owner and express finitely many equations and inequations in real coordinates.

For an affine chart, use compatible triangulation of a projective compactification, its boundary and the prescribed closed subvarieties. The noncompact open part has a finite CW homotopy model, not necessarily a compact finite realization. For a separated variety not assumed quasiprojective, choose a finite affine open cover; its intersections are affine and finite-cover descent reduces finiteness to these charts.
Consume the existing CW/cohomology finite-generation theorem and extend coefficients to Q. A simultaneous triangulation also makes algebraic closed covers excisive.
The generic compatible semialgebraic triangulation proof is the explicit external gap recorded for this node; the current RealAlgebraicGeometry roadmap excludes triangulation.
acceptance: For X=Spec(Q(i)) over Q, H^0 has rational dimension two after the chosen embedding into C.
Nilpotent thickening of a pair does not change its complex point space.

nodes.title: Cohomological exactness and naturality before reconstruction
nodes.statement: For Z⊆Y⊆X closed algebraic subvarieties, transpose Tau Ceti’s homological sequence over Q to obtain the natural exact sequence …→H^i(X,Y)→H^i(X,Z)→H^i(Y,Z)→δ H^{i+1}(X,Y)→…. For a map of triples the square with the two δ maps commutes, with no sign change. Together with pullback and identities these maps define the existing singular-cohomology-representation of the pair diagram. These checks precede use of the universal category.

sources.locator: Definition 9.1.1, pp. 205–206; Proposition 2.1.4 and Corollary 2.1.5 (the pair and triple sequences), p. 32
sources.match: The pair representation includes functoriality arrows in the reversed geometric direction and the connecting arrows of triples.

proofSteps: Make the analytic maps into a native TopTriple and use the pinned homological δ from the outer pair to the inner pair.
Over a field Hom_Q(−,Q) is exact. Identify relative cohomology with the dual of relative homology using the imported universal-coefficient comparison.
Transpose all three exactness statements and the naturality square. The order of the two terms reverses, giving the displayed cohomological sequence.
Check the point/empty pair and (A¹,{0,1}) explicitly to fix degree zero and the boundary sign.
acceptance: For ∅⊆{0,1}⊆A¹, the cokernel of Q→Q², a↦(a,a), is H^1(A¹,{0,1})=Q.
For Z=Y the inner relative term is zero and the outer-to-total map is the identity.
A commuting map of triples induces a commuting δ square before any Nori lift is constructed.

nodes.title: Affine dimension bound in relative cohomology
nodes.statement: For an affine complex variety X of dimension n, its analytic space has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex of dimension at most n. Hence H^q(X;R)=0 for q>n for every constant coefficient ring R. For a closed subvariety Z⊆X, the same vanishing holds for H^q(X,Z;R), by reducing first to the components of X not contained in Z so that dim Z<n. The assertion concerns homotopy dimension, not the real dimension 2n of a smooth analytic locus.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.3.12 and Corollary 2.3.15, pp. 39–40
sources.match: The affine homotopy-dimension theorem gives the absolute and relative vanishing used by the direct Basic Lemma proof.

proofSteps: Use the affine analytic homotopy-dimension input named in the gap register; it is not a consequence of general triangulation or of finite CW type alone.
Remove components lying in Z using closed-cover excision. Apply the absolute affine bound to X and the smaller-dimensional closed part Z.
The long exact sequence of the pair gives the relative bound, including degree n+1.
acceptance: For affine curves there is no cohomology above degree one.
For (A¹,{0,1}) the degree-one group survives, showing the bound is sharp.
The projective line has H²≠0 and does not satisfy the affine bound.

nodes.title: A sourced proof of Nori's Basic Lemma
nodes.statement: Let k⊆C, let X be an affine reduced finite-type k-scheme of dimension n, and let W⊆X be closed of dimension <n. There is a closed Z⊇W of dimension <n with X∖Z smooth, H^q(X(C),Z(C);Z)=0 for q≠n, and H^n(X(C),Z(C);Z) finite free. The result implies the same concentration and a finite free top group for every constant coefficient ring. The empty variety is handled separately; n=0 permits Z=∅. This supplies the proof input of the existing basic-lemma node.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.5.2, pp. 45–46; Lemma 2.5.8 and direct proof in §2.5.2, pp. 47–49
sources.match: Resolution, a normal-crossings compactification with the swapped complement affine, and duality give concentration; coefficient variation proves freeness.

proofSteps: Enlarge W by the nonsmooth locus and by lower-dimensional irreducible components when necessary; this still has dimension <n in characteristic zero.

Use the specific compactification/normal-crossings and ample-hyperplane input requested from SF.4 (Lemma 2.5.8). Excision identifies the relative cohomology with that of a smooth compactification minus one boundary, relative to the other.

Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies the low degrees with high relative degrees of the pair with boundaries interchanged. The swapped complement is affine, so relative affine vanishing kills those degrees. The original X is affine and kills the degrees >n; its proper modification need not be affine.

Repeat over every prime field. Finiteness plus universal coefficients then exclude integral torsion in the top degree and give finite freeness. Obtain arbitrary constant coefficients by the coefficient-change theorem.
The normal-crossings arrangement and affine analytic bound are named inputs, not consequences of the universal property.
acceptance: For n=0, Z=∅ and H^0 is free on the complex points, including nontrivial Artin components.
For X=A¹ and W={0,1}, Z=W gives H^1=Z.
The hypothesis dim W<n is necessary: W=X forces the relative pair to be zero and cannot leave a smaller-dimensional Z.

nodes.title: Good algebraic filtrations
nodes.statement: A cellular filtration of an affine variety X of dimension n is a finite increasing sequence of closed reduced subvarieties ∅=F_{−1}X⊆F_0X⊆…⊆F_NX=X, for some N≥n, such that every step (F_iX,F_{i−1}X,i) is a very good pair in the sense of the canonical effective-pairs-diagram (HM17 Definition 9.2.1(2); Harrer Definition 4.2.1): F_iX∖F_{i−1}X is smooth and either dim F_iX=i and dim F_{i−1}X=i−1 with relative cohomology concentrated in degree i, or F_iX=F_{i−1}X of dimension less than i. For i≤n the first form is forced, so dim F_iX=i; repeated levels occur only above n, with zero relative cohomology, when varieties of different dimensions are filtered in one index range. The Basic Lemma makes every step integrally good as well, with finite free top group. The weaker conditions dim F_iX≤i, smooth differences and concentration do not suffice: they admit good steps that are not very good, whose terms are not vertices of VGood. One may enlarge a prescribed dimension-bounded filtration to one of this form. Such filtrations exist by descending application of the Basic Lemma; compatible filtrations for a finite acyclic diagram of morphisms exist after enlargement.

sources.locator: Proposition 9.2.3 and Corollary 9.2.4, pp. 210–211
sources.match: Successive applications of the Basic Lemma give filtrations and compatible enlargements.

sources.locator: Definition 4.2.1, p. 128
sources.match: The steps of a cellular filtration are very good pairs, which is what places the cellular complex in the very-good-pair diagram category.

proofSteps: Construct F_{n−1} containing the prescribed closed subset by the Basic Lemma, then descend dimension. Insert repeated zero relative levels when a dimension is skipped.

For a finite acyclic diagram, order the objects and include the closures of images of already chosen lower stages. A morphism does not increase the dimension of its image; apply the prescribed-filtration version.
Common enlargement of two filtrations gives comparison maps of their cellular complexes. These are not claims about a universally chosen functorial filtration.
acceptance: Every level is a closed algebraic subvariety, not a topological skeleton.
The degree of a relative term is its filtration index, so one cannot put the whole variety in degree zero indiscriminately.
Every step is a vertex of the canonical very-good-pair diagram, not merely a good pair.

nodes.title: The complex attached to a good filtration
nodes.statement: In C(VGood,H_B), a cellular filtration F of X gives the cochain complex C_F^i(X)=H_N^i(F_iX,F_{i−1}X). Its differential is the connecting map for F_{i−1}⊆F_i⊆F_{i+1}. The square of the differential is zero by triple exactness and naturality. Maps of filtered varieties give contravariant cochain maps. The Betti image is naturally quasi-isomorphic, in the derived category, to relative/absolute singular cochains of the corresponding filtered variety; a strict natural cochain equivalence is not asserted.

The comparison is a derived comparison with a constructed map or zigzag.

nodes.title: Finite affine cover and filtration data
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type variety X choose a finite ordered affine open cover U_i. Its strictly increasing-index Čech terms are the finite disjoint unions U_{i_0}∩…∩U_{i_p}. These intersections are affine because X is separated, and the normalized cover direction is bounded by the number of opens. A cover-filtration consists of this cover and compatible cellular filtrations of the intersection diagram. For a finite acyclic geometric diagram, covers and filtrations can be chosen simultaneously after affine refinement. Pullbacks of affine opens along arbitrary morphisms are refined by affine opens; they are not assumed affine. A refinement is witnessed by a map of index sets, which is not unique (HM17 Example 9.2.6): two such maps induce cochain maps of the totalizations that agree up to an explicit Čech prism homotopy once filtrations compatible with the homotopy diagram are chosen. HM17 rigidifies the cover instead (Definition 9.2.7), which makes refinement maps unique (Remark 9.2.8); one of the two devices is used before comparison maps are composed.

nodes.title: Choice-independent realization and comparison of pair diagrams
nodes.statement: There is a contravariant realization on bounded complexes of separated varieties with formal Q-linear combinations of morphisms, valued in the bounded derived category of C(VGood,H_B). On an affine filtration it is C_F; on a general variety it is the affine-cover totalization. Choice comparisons are canonical derived isomorphisms satisfying identity, cocycle and naturality. Define R(X,Y)=Cone(R(X)→R(Y))[−1]. Its cohomology gives a representation of all pairs extending the original very-good-pair representation. Hence C(VGood,H_B)→C(Good,H_B)→C(Pairs,H_B) are equivalences. The natural sequence of a triple and the sequence with supports are represented motivically.

For two choices use a common affine cover refinement followed by a common enlargement of filtrations on a single finite diagram. Invert the constructed quasi-isomorphisms. A third simultaneous choice proves the cocycle law and independence of the intermediate cover.

Use simultaneous choices for a morphism, a composite and a homotopy. Their chain relations descend to the derived category; one must not infer existence or equality of motivic maps merely from equality of vector spaces.
Take cones for pairs. The cone identity for a nested triple yields R(X,Y)→R(X,Z)→R(Y,Z)→R(X,Y)[1], so its long cohomology sequence has the required δ.

On a general pair, R has all its cohomology groups; no concentration is assumed.

nodes.title: The good-pair diagram with inverse excision edges
nodes.statement: Let Good be the canonical diagram of effective good pairs of effective-pairs-diagram (rational concentration), represented by rational singular cohomology; HM17 Definition 9.2.1 asks for integral concentration with free top group, a full subdiagram with the same diagram category, and every statement below holds for either. Form Good_ex by adjoining the inverse of the cohomological restriction (S,T,n)→(S∖U,T∖U,n) whenever U is open in S and contained in T, with the representation assigning actual inverses to the new edges. The restriction is an isomorphism by algebraic closed-pair excision. In the diagram category its inverse already exists; hence C(Good_ex,H_B)≃C(Good,H_B), compatibly with fibres. For a boundary (Y,Z,n)→(X,Y,n+1) and a good pair (A,B,m), put S=Y×A∪X×B and T=Z×A∪X×B. The inverse excision edge from (Y×A,Z×A∪Y×B,n+m) to (S,T,n+m), followed directly by the boundary of X×A⊇S⊇T, defines the product boundary. Both endpoints of this boundary are good. It is unnecessary to pass through (S,Z×A∪Y×B,n+m), which need not be a good pair. The second-factor product (A,B,m)×∂ is defined in the same way with the factors exchanged. For very good inputs with B≠∅ the excision target (S,T,n+m) is good but not very good, because dim T=dim S, so these product paths live in Good_ex and not in the very-good diagram (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E74).

Excision identifies H*(S,T) with the source product pair, so this intermediate pair is good. Künneth identifies the boundary target with the product of the other two good vertices.

Construct the inverse excision map already in C(Good,H_B), since a faithful exact functor reflects isomorphisms. Each such inverse is present at the same finite diagram containing the original isomorphism, so no uncontrolled limit is needed.
The marked universal property supplies functors in both directions between the original and enlarged diagram categories; generation and compatibility show they are inverse.
Use Good_ex for the tensor proof. Transfer the resulting tensor structure to the equivalent very-good-pair category; do not require a product on the raw very-good-pair quiver.

The abelian category and its coalgebra description are preserved up to canonical fibre-compatible equivalence.
For very good factors with B≠∅, (S,T,n+m) satisfies dim T=dim S, so it is not a very good vertex; the tensor structure reaches C(VGood,H_B) only through the diagram-category equivalence.

nodes.title: Tensor structure from finite coefficient maps
nodes.statement: The Nori coalgebra of good pairs, after the inverse-excision completion, is a commutative bialgebra. Its multiplication is dual to the finite endomorphism-algebra maps induced by products of diagram vertices and generator maps. The native tensor product on finite right comodules therefore makes effective Nori motives a symmetric Q-linear abelian tensor category, with faithful exact tensor Betti functor. For the usual cohomological cross product κ(a⊗b)=a×b, the underlying boundary products are δa×b on the first factor and a×δb on the second; the latter is (−1)^deg(a) times the geometric total-boundary path. The ordinary symmetry is (−1)^{nm} times geometric interchange on degree n,m vertices. Equivalently, for the source convention τ^{-1}(a⊗b)=(−1)^{nm}a×b, a first-factor edge of parity r contributes (−1)^{rm}, and a second-factor edge contributes no sign.

sources.locator: Definition 8.1.3 and Proposition 8.1.5, pp. 180–183; corrected Proposition 9.3.1 and Theorem 9.3.4, pp. 222–225

proofSteps: Construct products of pullback generators geometrically. Construct boundary products by the preceding node and the cochain Leibniz rule. Inverse excision generators tensor to inverse excision isomorphisms. All constructions have finite support.

For finite diagrams F,G choose a finite H containing their products and all product paths. Endomorphisms of H act on the external tensor representation, giving E_H→E_F⊗E_G. The finite-dimensional identity End(T_F⊠T_G)=End(T_F)⊗End(T_G) follows by expressing the edge conditions as kernels and using exactness of tensor over a field.
Dualize to E_F∨⊗E_G∨→E_H∨ and pass to the filtered colimit. At a common finite stage, product coherence and units give the bialgebra identities; finite support descent makes choices independent.
Apply the existing finite-comodule tensor and symmetry machinery. The explicit sign transport is needed to turn graded geometric interchange into the ordinary symmetry seen by the fibre functor.
Tensor is exact in each variable because the fibre functor is faithful exact, its tensor comparison is an isomorphism, and tensoring vector spaces is exact.
acceptance: Two boundary generators give the Koszul interchange sign before the sign-corrected tensor is formed.
On a degree-one class the geometric factor swap is negative, while the fibre of the categorical symmetry is the ordinary flip.
The tensor unit is H_N^0(Spec Q)=Q and Künneth is realized by an actual motivic map.

nodes.title: Tensor inversion of the Nori Lefschetz object
nodes.statement: Let L=H_N^1(G_m,{1})=Q_N(−1) in effective Nori motives. The existing localization at L is equivalent to the diagram category obtained by adjoining all integer Tate twists to the corrected good-pair diagram, and to finite comodules over the coefficient bialgebra localized at the group-like coefficient of L. The Betti functor extends with ω_B(L)=Q, and L becomes tensor-invertible. Effective→full Nori motives is faithful exact; fullness is not asserted. The ungraded symmetry on L⊗L is the identity even though its geometric degree-one factor swap acts by −1.

Identify the localized coefficient with the group-like coefficient of L and extend coactions. Negative twists are dual powers of the rank-one object.

The objects Q_N(j) satisfy Q_N(i)⊗Q_N(j)≅Q_N(i+j) for all integers, including negative ones.
The proof never uses fullness of the effective inclusion.

nodes.title: Duality on generators and rigidity
nodes.statement: Over Q with rational coefficients the full Nori category is rigid, and its Betti functor is a neutral fibre functor. For the normal-crossings generator H_N^n(X,Y), with (X,Y)=(W∖D_∞,D_0∖D_∞) from a smooth projective n-dimensional W, its dual is H_N^n(W∖D_0,D_∞∖D_0)(n). The coevaluation is constructed by the diagonal class and Gysin maps with supports; its Betti dual pairing is perfect by Poincaré–Lefschetz duality. Generators and subquotient rigidity extend this to every object. In particular, for any algebraic pair (X,Y), the dual object of H_N^i(X,Y) has Betti realization H_i(X(C),Y(C);Q) by finite-dimensional universal coefficients. Dualizing the cohomological triple sequence gives the natural exact homological triple sequence, with connecting map from degree i+1 of (X,Y) to degree i of (Y,Z). For disconnected varieties all statements are componentwise: top cohomology is not asserted to be a single Tate object without geometric connectedness/irreducibility.

sources.match: Normal-crossings generators carry geometric perfect pairings, and the rigidity criterion propagates duals through generated subquotients.

sources.locator: Lemma 1.13 and Theorem 1.14, p. 8; Appendix C, Proposition C.4, pp. 27–28

proofSteps: Use resolution/principalization and an affine-bundle replacement to obtain the existing normal-crossings generator statement; these geometric inputs are part of the SF.4 request.

Retain the rational Artin H^0 object and its trace: the diagonal need not split into geometrically connected components over Q. Check the existing Gysin construction on complex components and descend the total diagonal class; do not replace the Artin factor by a rank-one Tate object.
Construct coevaluation via the support map from the diagonal into the product pair, and the tensor comparison already established. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality makes its fibre a perfect pairing.

Use the existing rigidity criterion over Q. The antipode/strong-dual identities propagate through finite sums and subquotients because the fibre is exact and finite-dimensional. Dualize the previously constructed pair objects and triple maps to obtain the homological exports, with the underlying Betti identification supplied by universal coefficients. Do not claim rigidity of the effective category.

For Spec Q(i), H^0 has rank two; a rank-one Tate replacement fails.
Coevaluation and evaluation satisfy both triangle identities after the faithful Betti functor.

nodes.title: Relative de Rham data required by the Nori fibre extension
nodes.statement: Over Q, the geometric input to the de Rham Nori fibre is a functor on algebraic pairs (X,Y,n)↦H_dR^n(X,Y/Q), with pullback, triple boundary, finite dimension, products, unit, integer Tate twist, and a natural comparison H_dR^n(X,Y/Q)⊗_Q C≅H_B^n(X,Y;Q)⊗_Q C compatible with all these maps. For arbitrary singular pairs the de Rham object is defined by smooth proper hypercover descent or the h-topology and the shifted cone for Y→X; it is not the naive Kähler complex of a singular scheme. This is the exact input contract to the already-owned MC.6/fibre-functor-extension. Its existence beyond the current smooth/proper and curve comparisons is an explicitly recorded supplier gap.

proofSteps: Consume the existing smooth de Rham complex, proper comparison and product/trace interface from ComplexComparisonPartII.

The missing extension must construct smooth proper hypercovers of a pair, prove cohomological descent and independence, and transport the shifted-cone boundary and multiplicative comparisons. The h-topological construction in the source is an alternative with the same contract.

Do not infer the arbitrary-pair comparison from the current C5 smooth proper theorem. Record the extension as a distinct proposed continuation of that roadmap and keep this stage planned until its owner is installed.

For Y=X the shifted cone is acyclic, so all relative groups vanish.
The node is a geometric supplier contract, not a second construction of abstract fibre-functor extension.

nodes.statement: Using the relative geometric de Rham input, the existing MC.6 fibre-functor extension gives an exact faithful tensor functor ω_dR:MM_Nori(Q,Q)→Vect_fd(Q), the existing exact faithful tensor Betti functor ω_B:MM_Nori(Q,Q)→Vect_fd(Q), and a tensor natural comparison ω_dR(−)⊗_Q C≅ω_B(−)⊗_Q C. All integer twists, evaluation and coevaluation are included. Both are neutral rational fibre functors. The existing canonical Nori definitions and MC.6 extension are used over Q; extending the motivic base field is outside this pass.

sources.match: Comparison-valued representations extend by marked universality and the rank-one Tate localization.

proofSteps: Form the abelian comparison category of two finite rational vector spaces with an isomorphism over C. Its Betti projection is faithful exact because C is faithfully flat over Q.
Apply the already-owned fibre extension to the pair representation, then the tensor comparison on good generators and uniqueness extend it to the category.
The inverse Lefschetz object maps to the dual rank-one comparison object, so the construction extends to every integer twist and respects duality.

For a negative Tate twist, comparison is the inverse power of the Lefschetz scalar.
The comparison commutes with triple boundaries, not merely with pullbacks.

nodes.title: The Tate pair and its normalized period
nodes.statement: For (G_m,{1}) over Q, H_B^1(G_m,{1};Q) is one-dimensional and maps isomorphically to H_B^1(G_m;Q); H_B^0(G_m,{1};Q)=0. The de Rham degree-one class is dz/z, its Betti dual generator is the counterclockwise unit loop, and the comparison pairing has value 2πi. Thus the Lefschetz comparison matrix is (2πi), its inverse twist has scalar (2πi)^{-1}, and integer tensor powers have (2πi)^r. No formal-period algebra or transcendence statement is constructed here.

Use the curve residue/comparison input for dz/z and the counterclockwise loop, with the complex exponential normalization.
Tensor compatibility and the explicit inverse-object evaluation determine every integer power.

For the constant degree-zero point object, the comparison scalar is 1.
The scalar is attached to specified rational and de Rham generators, not determined by dimensions alone.

nodes.title: The sheaf input to equivariant Nori filtrations
nodes.statement: Let k⊆C be a subfield (k=Q in the motivic application), Λ a ring, X an affine k-variety of dimension n and W⊂X closed of dimension <n. Let F be a weakly constructible sheaf of Λ-modules on X(C): locally constant on the members of a finite stratification by locally closed k-subvarieties (HM17 Definition 2.5.5). There is a dense Zariski open j:U⊆X∖W defined over k, with complement of dimension <n, such that H^q(X(C),j!j*F)=0 for q≠n and H^n(X(C),j!j*F) is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of stalks of F at points of U(C). A finite family of such sheaves has a common choice of U, by applying the statement to their direct sum. If the stalks of F are finite free over Λ (Λ=Z or Q and F constructible with free stalks, say), the top group is finite free. This stronger statement is the input for quotient-invariant filtrations; it is not inferred from the constant-sheaf Basic Lemma.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.5.7, p. 47; Nori’s proof in §2.5.3, Lemmas 2.5.9–2.5.11 and Theorem 2.5.12, pp. 49–52
sources.match: The Noether-normalization and coordinate-projection induction gives concentration and identifies the top group as a finite sum of stalks.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.3.8, p. 132, and the proof of Theorem 4.4.3, pp. 134–136
sources.match: The coefficient-linear form and its simultaneous use for quotient sheaves give the precise equivariant input.

proofSteps: Replace F by extension by zero from X∖W, then use Noether normalization to reduce along a finite map to affine n-space. The pinned algebraic normalization theorem supplies a finite injective polynomial-algebra map, not the identification of its number of variables with dimension; the dimension/finite-Spec adapter is part of the recorded supplier gap.

On affine n-space enlarge the bad locus to a hypersurface and choose a coordinate projection whose restriction to that hypersurface is finite and surjective. Its coefficient sheaf vanishes on the hypersurface and is locally constant on the complement.

Use the variation of base change in Theorem 2.5.12, not unrestricted base change for a nonproper projection. Its exact hypothesis is that the ambient map is a locally trivial topological fibre bundle and the non-locally-constant locus is proper over the base. Fibrewise, retract a punctured affine line onto a finite embedded tree whose vertices are the bad points; its relative sheaf cohomology is in degree one and is a finite sum of stalks on the edges.

Algebraic stratification of the branch locus makes R¹π_*F locally constant on strata and all other direct images vanish. Induct on dimension and use the Leray spectral sequence to obtain the displayed concentration and top group. The analytic constructibility/base-change/stratification adapters are exact missing inputs in the supplier gap.
Use a direct sum to impose the same open set for the finite collection of quotient sheaves required by the equivariant proof.
acceptance: For a zero-dimensional X, the assertion is the finite direct sum of its stalks in degree zero.
For F the constant Z-sheaf on A¹, with W={0,1}, U=A¹∖W gives H¹=Z.
The map π need not be proper; base change is used only with its proper bad locus and fibre-bundle hypotheses.

nodes.title: Equivariant cellularity and finite quotient invariants
nodes.statement: Let a finite group G act by Q-scheme automorphisms on an affine Q-variety X. Given a finite standard filtration G_i(X), with dim G_i(X)≤i, there is a larger G-invariant standard filtration F_i(X), dim F_i(X)≤i, which is integrally cellular, whose quotient filtration on X/G is integrally cellular, and for which quotient pullback is an isomorphism C•_(F/G)(X/G)≅C•_F(X)^G in effective Nori motives. Invariants are the kernel of the finite family of maps g−id in the existing abelian category. At each stage any prescribed lower-dimensional closed subset can be included. The same construction gives nice filtrations at the disjoint, isolated quotient arrows of a finite acyclic diagram, under the endpoint and no-intervening-object conditions of Harrer Lemma 4.4.7.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.3.8, p. 132; Lemmas 4.4.1–4.4.2, pp. 132–133; Theorems 4.4.3 and 4.4.5, pp. 134–137; Definition 4.4.6 and Lemma 4.4.7, pp. 137–138
sources.match: Constructible-sheaf vanishing yields simultaneous good pairs upstairs and downstairs, with quotient pullback identifying invariant cohomology and then Nori complexes.

proofSteps: For the finite quotient π:X→X/G, pushforward of analytic sheaves is exact by proper base change and finite fibres. On every orbit the kernel of the difference maps into the product over G is the constant diagonal subgroup; its image and cokernel have finite free integral stalks by Lemma 4.4.2.

Apply the preceding constructible-sheaf Basic Lemma over Z simultaneously to extension by zero of the constant sheaf, its finite pushforward, and the image/cokernel difference sheaves. This gives a dense open complement where all their relative cohomology is concentrated in the top degree. Its proof adapters are recorded in the geometric supplier gap. Integral concentration with free top group implies rational concentration, so every step is a vertex of the canonical (rational) very-good-pair diagram; the integral form is what Harrer proves and is not needed beyond this.

The two exact sequences identify integral relative cohomology of the quotient with the G-invariants upstairs; extension to Q commutes with these finite kernels. Include the nonsmooth loci upstairs and the inverse image of the nonsmooth locus downstairs in the prescribed bad subset. Pull the closed complement back to obtain an invariant closed subset containing it, and induct on dimension to obtain the filtrations with smooth successive differences.

The quotient pullback is an actual morphism of Nori complexes. Its factorization through the invariant kernels is checked by faithful Betti realization; exactness identifies their fibres, and conservativity proves it is an isomorphism.

For the diagram version assume each chosen quotient arrow has endpoints disjoint from those of every other chosen quotient, is the only arrow between its endpoints, and has no factorization through a third object. Induct by terminal quotient pairs, keeping a previously fixed initial segment when it contains both or neither endpoint of each quotient arrow.
acceptance: For the trivial group, quotient pullback is the identity cellular complex.

For the transitive G-set G/H, where H is a point stabilizer, regarded as a finite reduced split scheme, H^0 of the quotient is the diagonal Q inside Q^(G/H), and pullback identifies it with invariants.
The quotient map and invariants commute with the cellular differential; an invariant choice of individual vector spaces alone does not satisfy the theorem.

nodes.title: Finite correspondences on cellular Nori complexes
nodes.statement: For smooth affine Q-varieties X,Y, an integral finite correspondence α:X↝Y determines, after compatible cellular filtrations and enlargement, a contravariant map of Nori cellular complexes. A finite correspondence is a finite Q-linear combination of integral closed subvarieties of X×Y finite and surjective over a connected component of X. The map is defined by the associated multivalued morphism and the invariant finite-cover trace, with its multiplicities; it is additive in α and extends graph pullback. Its cohomological Betti map is the usual correspondence action. This construction uses the finite-correspondence carrier of MC.4/M.5a and the symmetric-power/trace geometry requested below; no replacement category of correspondences is introduced.

sources.locator: Theorems 3.7.5 and 3.7.7, pp. 114–116; Definition 4.6.2 and Lemmas 4.6.1/4.6.3 and Propositions 4.7.1–4.7.2, pp. 140–144
sources.match: Multivalued morphisms encode finite correspondences and induce compatible, eventually additive cellular maps, including multiplicities.

proofSteps: On a connected smooth X, encode an effective correspondence of degree d by X→Sym^d(Y); subtract effective parts only after constructing the additive action. Smoothness gives normality, the hypothesis of the multivalued-morphism comparison. Clear the finitely many rational denominators to choose integral cellular refinements for the finitely many effective integral constituents; extend the resulting maps Q-linearly only after additivity.

Choose an admissible filtration preserved by the correspondence. Construct the map through symmetric powers and rational invariants/trace as in §4.6; the transfer is a sum over sheets and retains multiplicities.
An equality of two effective sums may require a larger filtration before the corresponding maps agree. Use Proposition 4.7.2 before group-completing, then extend Q-linearly.

nodes.title: Simultaneous filtration for correspondence relations
nodes.statement: Every finite hom-almost acyclic diagram of smooth affine Q-varieties and finite Q-correspondences admits compatible cellular filtrations after enlargement. Here the indexing category has finitely many objects and finite hom sets; arrows in both directions force the objects to coincide; each endomorphism monoid is a finite group; and these group elements act by graphs of actual scheme automorphisms. The resulting contravariant maps preserve composition, and all prescribed finite additive relations become equalities after a common enlargement. This includes diagrams encoding a composition, an additive relation, a chain-map equation and a chain homotopy. Product filtrations give external-product comparison maps compatible with these structures.

Use eventual additivity and Theorem 4.8.1 for composition. Induct over the finite partial order of objects, retaining already fixed source filtrations and enlarging the new terminal target. Finally enlarge it to be invariant under its finite automorphism group, as in Theorem 4.8.4.
For bounded complexes use their finite diagram of terms and components; the relations d²=0 and d f=f d are among the finite relations. Apply the same construction to the finite diagram of a homotopy.

The product filtration has level n equal to the union of F_i(X)×G_j(Y) over i+j=n. Field Künneth and relative Mayer–Vietoris give its cellularity and the tensor-complex comparison. Product filtrations need not be final among all filtrations (Remark 4.9.5), so permit arbitrary common enlargements when comparing choices. nodes.title: Cellular Nisnevich covers for correspondences
nodes.statement: A cellular cover-filtration for a finite acyclic diagram in SmCor(Q,Q) consists of compatible affine, unifibrantly c-rigidified cd-Nisnevich covers of all vertices, with chosen componentwise lifts of its correspondence edges, and compatible cellular filtrations of the resulting Čech correspondence diagram. The lift includes bridge data specifying the correspondence over pairs of covering schemes and its compatibility with composition. Such covers exist over Q. The extra rigidification selects lifts consistently under composition, and a cd-cover is a finite composite of covers from elementary Nisnevich distinguished squares (Harrer Definition 5.3.1, p. 170). Unifibrancy means that each base point has a chosen covering member whose fibre is a single point with the same residue field; c-rigidification chooses such points constructibly and meets every connected component (Definition 6.1.1, pp. 179–180). Covers are chosen first and filtrations second. The total Nori complex is initially bounded below; its bounded cohomology makes it an object of the bounded derived category. The collection of combined cover-filtrations is connected by comparison zigzags, not asserted to be a directed poset.

Form the finite Čech diagram of isomorphism classes of connected components over each base, using chosen representatives. Despite the unbounded repeated-index Čech complex, this diagram has finitely many objects and finite hom sets and is hom-almost acyclic: use Proposition 5.5.7, pp. 176–177, and Proposition 6.6.3, pp. 194–195. This finite diagram, rather than the full infinite set of Čech occurrences, is the input to the simultaneous-filtration theorem.

Only now choose compatible cellular filtrations on that finite diagram and induce them on every Čech term using Theorem 6.6.2, p. 194. Totalize in the bounded-below shape of Definition 7.1.5; conjugate the source differential by the specified sign before using our convention. A repeated-index Čech direction is not bounded.
The existence proof needs the precise cover-lifting/bridge geometry in the supplier gap. Ordinary open-cover pullback alone does not lift a finite correspondence.

nodes.title: Comparison maps for cover-filtration choices
nodes.statement: For a bounded complex X• of smooth varieties with finite correspondences, and any two cellular Nisnevich cover-filtrations F,G, there is a derived isomorphism φ_FG:C_G(X•)≅C_F(X•). It is independent of auxiliary common covers and filtration enlargements, satisfies φ_FF=id and φ_FG φ_GH=φ_FH, and is natural for maps of complexes of correspondences. Each isomorphism is a zigzag of explicitly constructed refinement quasi-isomorphisms. The derived Betti functor detects these quasi-isomorphisms but is not used to invent maps.

Construct the comparison maps of total complexes. Their Betti maps are quasi-isomorphisms by Čech descent and the cellular comparison.
For any two auxiliary choices choose a common further covering refinement, then enlarge all filtrations in the resulting finite diagram. The resulting commutative diagram proves independence.
Repeat with three choices for the cocycle and with a morphism for naturality. The fibre is faithful exact, hence its derived functor conservative; fullness is neither needed nor available.

nodes.title: Effective geometric motives have Nori realization
nodes.statement: Over Q there is a contravariant triangulated tensor functor R_N^eff:DM_gm^eff(Q,Q)→D^b(MM_Nori^eff(Q,Q)). On a smooth X its Betti image computes RΓ_sing(X(C),Q); on the relative motive Cone(M(Y)→M(X)) of a very good pair (X,Y,n) with X and Y smooth, its value is H_N^n(X,Y)[−n]. It extends the graph-only variety realization, is compatible with finite correspondences and carries the affine-line homotopy and Nisnevich Mayer–Vietoris relations to zero. Tensor compatibility is the natural external-product comparison of the constructed complexes. No equivalence of the two categories is asserted.

conventions.totalization: On bidegree (i,j), use d=d_first+(-1)^i d_second. Harrer Convention 1.1.3, pp. 18–19, uses d_H=d_second+(-1)^j d_first. Multiplication by (-1)^(ij) is the chain isomorphism from our total complex to his. Conjugate all cited double-totalization and tensor comparisons by this map, and iterate for three directions. Cochain shifts satisfy H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A); the contravariant realization reverses shifts.
